title: The Veiled Blade and Lord Valthalak
summary: Anthion seeks the rescue of Ysida from Stratholme; afterward, the Veiled Blade’s divided amulet draws an adventurer through its scattered companions to Valthalak’s old lair.
opening: Two faction paths lead to one ghost outside Stratholme. His request begins with a rescue; the road beyond it uncovers an old mercenary company, a broken medallion, and the danger its members left behind.

chapters.title: A Rescue Beyond Death
chapters.body:
From Ironforge or Orgrimmar, separate appeals led seekers toward the same old wound. Beyond Stratholme waited Anthion Harmon’s ghost. Armor and its improvement had opened the journey, but a deeper burden lay ahead: a captive wife, a company’s last contract, and a medallion whose divided pieces carried more than any of their owners had understood.

Beside the Eastern Plaguelands road, a goblin device let the living hear Anthion Harmon. Death had not quieted his concern. Baron Rivendare held Ysida, his wife, inside Stratholme; Anthion had tried to reach her and failed. Behind the bare branches and grey-green haze rose the city. Within it waited the question that still bound him: whether Ysida lived.

Anthion’s plea carried two losses at once. He had died trying to reach Ysida, yet the fear of losing her still held him beside the road. He asked that another finish the rescue. Beyond his restless spirit, Stratholme sheltered the danger he had been unable to overcome. Hope endured there only while his wife could still be brought beyond the Baron’s reach.

The way through Stratholme led to the Slaughter House, where Rivendare held Ysida. Amid walls steeped in the Scourge’s corruption, the rescuers reached her alive and brought her beyond his grasp. The city’s horror had not taken her. Now a message could be carried back to the husband she believed lost, answering the fear that had kept his spirit upon the road.

Ysida gave the rescuer her locket to carry to Anthion, proof that she remained alive. When it reached the roadside ghost, he learned that the rescue had succeeded. Their reunion was divided by death, yet her survival released him from the fear that held him there. The token of a living wife brought peace to a husband who could no longer return to her.

chapters.title: Anthion and Theldren
chapters.body:
Anthion turned toward the Veiled Blade’s spoils. The company had divided a medallion among its plunder without understanding its importance. Theldren, a dwarf, had taken the top piece. Anthion had tried to win it back and suffered a harsh defeat. Another challenger would have to recover it, and the old company’s scattered treasure began to reveal a burden greater than greed.

In Dire Maul’s Athenaeum, Falrin Treeshaper heard the request from his old friend. He had believed Anthion dead. Now he agreed to prepare an enchantment that could draw Theldren into a fight. Falrin’s anger at the ogres carried the memory of his brother’s death. Amid the ancient halls, an old bond offered the means to reach a fragment that Anthion could not reclaim himself.

Beneath Blackrock Mountain, the challenge reached the Ring of Law. As High Justice Grimstone pronounced sentence, the intruders planted Falrin’s banner. Theldren answered the provocation and entered with his gladiators. The battle yielded the top piece of the medallion. What had been divided among the company could now begin to return, though the whereabouts of the remaining fragments still lay with its scattered companions.

Anthion explained what the Veiled Blade had learned too late. They had broken Valthalak’s amulet into three parts out of greed, unaware that it held much of the warlock’s soul. A curse had followed. He sent the seeker toward Bodley, who could guide the recovery of the other pieces. The rescued husband’s gratitude became a plea to repair the company’s wrong.

chapters.title: The Company of Fragments
chapters.body:
Near Blackrock Spire’s entrance balcony, Bodley’s ghost waited. He had returned toward the fortress and never come back alive. With the top fragment recovered, he could point toward the other pieces. His welcome carried warmth even beside the place where the danger had begun. Death had left him with knowledge, and with the wish that another might undo what the company had done.

Bodley remembered the commission from Gremnik Rizzlesprang, a goblin smuggler-wizard of Booty Bay. The Veiled Blade had been hired to steal Lord Valthalak’s spellbook from Blackrock Spire. Whether Gremnik meant to study it or sell it, Bodley did not know. The company had accepted the work without understanding the power of the lord whose possession they intended to take.

Before Drakkisath, Valthalak had served as Blackrock Spire’s general, a drakonid noble and warlock. The Veiled Blade entered the upper fortress, slew him and took his spellbook. They knew too little of his power over souls to understand what they had disturbed. In the lair later called the Beast’s chamber, their successful theft opened the way to their ruin.

As the company prepared to leave, Kormok claimed Valthalak’s amulet. The quarrel nearly brought them to blows. They broke it into three pieces and divided them by lot, learning only later how much of his spirit it held. Theldren’s fragment had already returned through Anthion’s challenge. The others carried the consequences of that quarrel into the scattered lives of their owners.

Valthalak rose as a spirit and called spectral assassins against the mercenaries. Their struggle roused the Spire’s defenders. Most of the Veiled Blade escaped, but the assassins followed wherever they hid. The company broke apart beneath a curse that pursued each shard. Amid the confusion, Mor Grayhoof fell toward the fortress’s lower reaches, beginning another loss the survivors would remember.

Mor Grayhoof survived the fall into Lower Blackrock Spire. Trolls captured him, and War Master Voone tortured him. Valthalak’s spectral assassins finished what the fall had not. His fate became one of the haunted memories left by the company’s flight. The fortress that had yielded its plunder now held another of those who had taken it.

Kormok turned toward Scholomance. The two-headed ogre had been drawn to necromancy, with a cold and clever mind beside a more foolish one. After the company scattered, he sought further study in that dark place. Valthalak’s spectral assassins reached him there and killed him before Ras Frostwhisper. His new pursuit had offered no refuge from the old curse.

Isalien travelled to Dire Maul, seeking answers about her night elf heritage and perhaps the magic within her fragment. Bodley remembered her friendship with Falrin. In the old kaldorei halls, Alzzin the Wildshaper and his forces ambushed her. The company’s scattered history had reached another haunted place, where a search for knowledge met the danger that followed its plunder.

Jarien and Sothos sought knighthood in the Scarlet Crusade at Stratholme. When Sothos failed the final trial, Jarien defended her brother and demanded that they be admitted together. Grand Crusader Dathrohan killed them both. The amulet piece further twisted their spirits. Their hope of a new allegiance had ended in death, and the company’s burden endured beyond it.

Bodley guided the search among the places haunted by his former companions. Different seekers faced different spirits, but the fragments belonged to the same broken amulet and the same ruined company. With the missing pieces recovered and joined to Theldren’s top fragment, the medallion could become whole again. Its restoration would bring the search back to the owner whose wrath had followed them.

chapters.title: Return the Spirit
chapters.body:
Bodley prepared a brazier to call Valthalak in his old lair. Its making drew upon the haunted places where the company’s companions had fallen. Their scattered fates had brought the search near its end. In the Beast’s chamber, the brazier would offer the means to summon the warlock and confront the power that still pursued the broken company.

In the Beast’s chamber, the brazier called Valthalak into a body that could be fought. After his defeat, the restored amulet was placed upon his corpse, and his spirit appeared whole again. He recognized that the seeker had not belonged to the original thieves. He demanded his property back, and sent an answer to those whose theft had divided it.

Valthalak declared the Veiled Blade safe—for now. Bodley was astonished that the spirit would call off his assassins, though the promise still carried a warning. The company remained scattered among separate lives and deaths. Its lost fellowship could not be restored with the amulet. Yet the object was whole again, and for this moment the pursuit it had unleashed was ended.

reviewNote: Complete 22-scene illustrated research telling with 22 transcript-matched AI narration tracks, separate faction introductions, the Anthion/Ysida rescue, Theldren’s challenge, Bodley’s manual account, four explicitly alternative companion-fate scenes and the Valthalak finale. Main journey: original World of Warcraft Classic / Era 8. Quest text, manual lore, faction variants, and order are drawn from accessible secondary mirrors; capture and compare the original client/build before promotion. Bodley’s account stays attributed and Gremnik’s motive remains unknown. The four haunted-locus variants are an editorial memorial sequence, not four mandatory kills by one canonical character. Art is interpretive and its matching in-game area comparison remains a human review gate. No TBC, Wrath, or later character outcomes are added.
